solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A swan captured by woman of historic reign

indicators.note: the pieces before these words are held inside the name that follows

parts.note: Jean is a woman's name
a cob is a male swan

explanation.surface: A swan is caught by a woman at the time of some famous historical reign.
explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a male swan, a convention worth knowing; 'captured by' puts the swan inside the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the period of James I's rule, from Jacobus, the Latin form of James.

clue.text: Little woman kept missing gym — it makes you laugh

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women

indicators.note: says the gym letters are absent from the word kept

parts.note: PT, physical training, is school gym

explanation.surface: A young woman skipped her gym class, which is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: A gag or quip is told to amuse, making the listener laugh.

clue.text: Romancer's ex is abused? One must ask many questions

indicators.note: the words are mistreated, so their letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover's former partner is mistreated, and someone is bound to start asking questions.
explanation.definitionFit: In court, the lawyer questioning the other side's witness asks many probing questions.

clue.text: Support trainees working out problem

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: working the letters out means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: Backing apprentices as they solve a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like solving, but signals the anagram of trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that tests the mind is a problem to be solved.

clue.text: Clear account, pretty short

indicators.note: short means cut, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: pretty, as in pretty good, means quite

explanation.surface: A bank statement is clear and rather brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' is the adverb (pretty good) meaning QUITE, cut short to QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a defendant is to find them not guilty in court.

clue.text: American journalist is employed

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's standard journalist

explanation.surface: An American reporter has a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to work, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Roman Christian blasting a recent sin, keeping commandment

indicators.note: the jumble holds the next piece inside
the words are blown apart and their letters reassembled

parts.note: a law is a commandment

explanation.surface: A believer in Rome condemns a fresh wrong while observing a commandment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasting' rearranges A RECENT SIN to SAINTRENCE; 'keeping' places LAW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This third-century deacon of Rome was martyred there, a Christian saint of Rome.

clue.text: Fighter expected to join fifty on register

parts.note: due means expected, as a train due at noon
L is the Roman numeral fifty
a list is a register

explanation.surface: A combatant is due to sign up and add fifty to the roll.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fights formal single combat with swords or pistols is a fighter.

clue.text: Foreign money carried around by henchman or knight

indicators.note: the hidden run is turned the other way round to be read backwards
the letters are carried inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Some foreign cash is carried about by a heavy or a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried by' hides ANORK in 'henchmAN OR Knight'; 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Sweden and of Iceland is a foreign money unit with this name.

clue.text: One of five children at home given one drug or another

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five born together
in means at home
E is ecstasy, a single drug

explanation.surface: A quintuplet, home in bed, is handed one medicine or a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'another', meaning another drug, following on from 'one drug'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinine is a medicinal drug taken against malaria, so it is another drug besides ecstasy.

clue.text: Crazy niece, all but irresistable

indicators.note: crazy letters are out of their right order

explanation.surface: A mad niece is very nearly impossible to resist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' looks like 'nearly', but is just part of the fodder. The clue spells irresistible with an a.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be escaped or avoided is impossible to resist, a near synonym.

clue.text: Being slushy drove one mad

parts.note: drove someone mad, sent them round the bend: to send is to drive
the Roman numeral I is one
mental means mad, informally

explanation.surface: Being mawkish drove somebody crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' only links; the surface reads 'drove one mad' as one idiom, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Slushy writing is mushy and over-emotional, which is the same idea as mawkish and soppy.

clue.text: Models, very good, appearing in English books

indicators.note: the very good piece appears inside the next pieces

parts.note: tomes are big books
PI, short for pious, means very good

explanation.surface: Fashion models, really good, feature in English books.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal examples of a quality are perfect models of it.

clue.text: Little folk having food around nine or eleven

indicators.note: the food goes round the number placed inside it

parts.note: pies are food
IX is nine and XI is eleven in Roman numerals; either fits inside the pies to give the same letters

explanation.surface: Small people eat food around nine or eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: P(IX)IES and PI(XI)ES give the same letters, so the setter fairly offers either number.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixies are tiny mischievous sprites of folklore, a kind of little folk or fairy people.

clue.text: Invaders coming round in the morning, returning people

indicators.note: the invaders surround the piece placed inside them

parts.note: the Huns were invaders of the Roman Empire

indicators.note: says the morning abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: Raiders arrive around dawn and then go back to the people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming round' is the insertion signal and 'returning' the reversal of the morning abbreviation; the Huns are the classic crossword invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of mankind are people, as opposed to animals or aliens.

clue.text: A female has to worry about what to present wine in

indicators.note: the worry goes about the pieces placed inside it

parts.note: care is worry

explanation.surface: A woman must fret about how to serve wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jug with a narrow neck is used for serving wine at the table.

clue.text: A monster hat — alternatively a wee cap

indicators.note: taken in an alternative order, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hat like a monster, or else a little Scottish cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' is Scots for small, hinting at the Scottish cap.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Scottish woollen bonnet named after a Burns poem, a cap a Scot would wear.

clue.text: Enthusiasm shown by final character is French

parts.note: Z is the final letter of the alphabet
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: Keenness is shown by the last person, who happens to be French.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto, eager enjoyment, a synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Island child getting about

parts.note: a minor is a child in law
CA, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A child on an island is going around.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: For example, writer rolling around in orgy

indicators.note: the combined pieces roll round to be read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: An author is said to be rolling about at a debauched party.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spree of overindulgence, close to a drunken revel or wild party.

clue.text: Agile agent strangles traitor finally

indicators.note: the agent wraps tightly round the letter put inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word traitor

explanation.surface: A nimble operative throttles a turncoat at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone lively and nimble, especially when old, so agile is a synonym.

clue.text: Some love he-men, totally fierce

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people adore macho men, utterly ferociously.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement feelings are intense and forceful, much as a fierce attack is passionate.
